output.title: Event-driven data platform
output.description: Operational events stream through Kafka into Snowflake; dbt builds marts and reverse ETL publishes segments back to Kafka.

simulations.title: Follow one order end to end
simulations.description: One checkout travels through Kafka, Snowflake and dbt, then comes back out as a segment change.

action.text: A shopper checks out. Follow this one order through Kafka, Snowflake and dbt, and back out to Kafka as a segment change.
The Snowflake Kafka connector streams the event into a RAW table within about a second. There is no nightly batch window.
dbt's incremental models turn the raw row into marts. This order moves the customer into a new segment.
Reverse ETL compares the mart with its last sync and publishes only the changed row to customer-segments.v1.
Personalization and the marketing tool consume the change like any other event, each in its own consumer group.

expectations.label: dbt builds it into the marts

simulations.title: Warehouse load spike
simulations.description: Month-end invoices spike to 600/s on top of steady orders and CDC; Kafka absorbs the burst while the loader catches up.

action.text: Orders, invoices and account changes all stream into Snowflake. Each dot is 20 events. The connector loads about 600 rows a second.
Month-end: invoice webhooks jump to 600 a second. The loader falls behind, and Kafka absorbs the burst as consumer lag.
Producers never slowed down. Once the spike passes, the connector drains the lag and RAW catches up.
Only order-driven segment changes flow back out through reverse ETL. Invoices and account rows stay in the marts.

expectations.label: The loader falls behind during the spike
